rationale: No prior record of this pair exists: STRING found no association, CellPhoneDB found no curated interaction, and PubMed returned 0 co-mentions. The pair is biologically plausible, since both are cell-membrane proteins per UniProt (SLITRK2 Q9H156 single-pass, GPR22 Q99680 7-TM orphan GPCR) and both are brain-expressed per HPA. The structural support is weak, however: ipTM is 0.5, exactly at the threshold; interface pLDDT is 63.4; the supplied p_twoway is 0.057; both proteins carry 2 annotated glycosylation sites whose position relative to the interface could not be checked; and the membrane side of the interface is unverified. This is a novel, plausible hypothesis, not a supported interaction.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: UniProt marks both proteins as glycoproteins with 2 annotated glycosylation sites each. SLITRK2 additionally has 4 disulfide bonds and 1 modified residue and is a phosphoprotein. The PubMed PTM search returned 1 hit for SLITRK2 (PMID 27812321, on Slitrk missense mutations impairing trafficking and synapse formation) and 2 hits for GPR22, neither of which is about GPR22 glycosylation. Neither protein's function text describes a glycan- or lipid-mediated binding mechanism. Glycosylation sites on such proteins are typically extracellular, and the supplied interface is very large (buried surface area 6162 Å2, 1280 contacts), so overlap with a glycan site is possible. It could not be checked without per-residue interface data, so this is an unresolved caveat and not evidence of an artifact.
cooccurrence_evidence: PubMed co-occurrence for SLITRK2 and GPR22 returned 0 hits.
known_interaction_evidence: STRING returned no association for SLITRK2 and GPR22 (found: false). CellPhoneDB returned no curated interaction (found: false), and GPR22 is not in the CellPhoneDB gene table. PubMed co-occurrence returned 0 papers. There is no hit in any of the three sources, so the pair is novel.
follow_up: Folding was not available in this run. Recommended next steps: (1) Re-fold SLITRK2 with GPR22 and read the interface topology, to confirm the interface does not touch both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues at once; the very large buried surface area (6162 Å2) with a minimum separation of 1.37 Å and interface pLDDT of only 63.4 could reflect the SLITRK2 leucine-rich-repeat ectodomain wrapping or interleaving non-physically around the 7-TM bundle. (2) Check whether the 2 N-glycosylation sites on each protein fall on the interface, and if so re-fold with glycans attached. (3) Treat the fold itself as marginal until re-folded: ipTM is 0.5 and p_twoway is 0.057, although only 1 of the 4 receptors tested against this partner passed the confidence gate, which argues against a generically sticky partner. (4) If the fold holds up, test by co-immunoprecipitation or a cell-surface binding assay in neurons or HEK cells. NTRK2 is listed under other subunits only because UniProt says SLITRK2 negatively regulates it; it is not a curated complex member, and CellPhoneDB lists no complexes for either protein.

rationale: The pair is novel (no STRING record, no CellPhoneDB hit, 0 PubMed co-mentions) and both are plasma-membrane proteins, so a cis interaction is topologically possible. However, L1CAM (P32004) carries 20 annotated glycosylation sites on its ectodomain and GPR61 (Q9BZJ8) has 1 N-glycosylation site on its extracellular N-terminus. The modelled interface is very large (buried surface area 5999 Å2, 1330 contacts) but only modestly confident (interface pLDDT 55.9, ipTM 0.61). An interface of that size on L1CAM very probably covers glycan-bearing surface that AF3 did not model, and may also involve GPR61 surface that is buried in the lipid bilayer; neither could be checked without a fold. Expression overlap in HPA is also weak.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: UniProt annotates L1CAM (P32004) with the Glycoprotein and Phosphoprotein keywords, 20 glycosylation sites, 9 modified residues and 6 disulfide bonds. Given its single transmembrane helix, the glycosylation sites are expected to lie on the large extracellular Ig/FnIII ectodomain. UniProt annotates GPR61 (Q9BZJ8) as a Glycoprotein with 1 glycosylation site; PMID 29226084 ("N-glycosylation and expression in human tissues of the orphan GPR61 receptor") reports its N-glycosylation. The PubMed PTM search returned 85 hits for L1CAM and 2 for GPR61. An interface burying 5999 Å2 on a 20-site glycoprotein ectodomain is likely to overlap glycan positions, but the per-residue overlap was not checked because no fold could be run.
cooccurrence_evidence: PubMed co-occurrence for L1CAM and GPR61 returned 0 hits.
known_interaction_evidence: STRING returned no association for L1CAM and GPR61. CellPhoneDB returned no curated interaction, and GPR61 is not in the CellPhoneDB gene table. PubMed co-occurrence returned 0 papers. The pair is therefore novel as far as these sources show.
follow_up: A fold could not be run in this triage, so these are recommendations. (1) Re-fold L1CAM with GPR61 and read the structural analysis for interface topology on both chains and for whether L1CAM's N-glycosylation sites or the GPR61 N-terminal glycosylation site sit on the interface. If the interface touches both cytoplasmic and extracellular residues, or L1CAM ectodomain contacts the lipid-facing transmembrane surface of GPR61, treat it as an artifact. (2) If glycosylation sites are on the interface, re-fold with core N-glycans attached. (3) Consider folding only the L1CAM cytoplasmic tail against GPR61's intracellular loops and C-terminus, and separately the L1CAM Ig1-4 domains against the GPR61 N-terminus, to localise any real contact. (4) The supplied screen data show this partner was confident against only 1 of 6 receptors tested (p_twoway = 0.010437), which argues for some specificity; if the re-fold survives, test by co-immunoprecipitation or BRET in neuronal cells that express both. CellPhoneDB lists EZR as an L1CAM complex partner (pL1:Ezrin), which binds the cytoplasmic tail and is unlikely to be an obligate subunit for this pair.

rationale: The pair is novel by every database checked (STRING not found, CellPhoneDB not found, PubMed co-mention count 0), and both are cell-membrane proteins per UniProt, so an ectodomain-ectodomain contact is physically possible. However, the evidence cannot support a positive call: HPA has no subcellular localisation for either protein, the AF3 signal is borderline (ipTM 0.52, interface pLDDT 60.7), and without a fold analysis I cannot tell whether the modelled interface is on a topologically consistent side of the membrane or is covered by the 7 N-glycosylation sites annotated on NCR3LG1 (Q68D85) and the 2 on GPR179 (Q6PRD1). There is also no demonstrated biological context in which the retina/neuron-restricted GPR179 meets NCR3LG1.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: UniProt annotates NCR3LG1 as a Glycoprotein with 7 glycosylation sites and 2 disulfide bonds, and GPR179 as a Glycoprotein with 2 glycosylation sites and 2 disulfide bonds. The PubMed PTM/glycosylation search returned 0 hits for each gene, so there is no literature on specific sites from that tool. Seven glycosylation sites on a single-pass immunoglobulin-domain protein would normally lie on the ectodomain, which is the only part of NCR3LG1 that could plausibly contact GPR179's extracellular region, so glycan occlusion of the modelled interface is a real but unverified concern. Whether any site falls on the modelled contact residues could not be checked because no fold analysis was available in this run.
cooccurrence_evidence: PubMed co-occurrence for NCR3LG1 and GPR179 returned a count of 0 with no hits.
known_interaction_evidence: STRING returned no association for NCR3LG1 and GPR179 (found: false). CellPhoneDB has no curated interaction for the pair, and GPR179 is not in the CellPhoneDB gene table at all, so that miss is uninformative for GPR179. PubMed co-occurrence returned 0 papers. The pair is therefore unreported. The only documented function of NCR3LG1 in UniProt is triggering NCR3-dependent natural killer cell activation; GPR179 is an orphan receptor documented to associate with R7 RGS-GNB5 complexes, TRPM1 and GRM6.
follow_up: 1) Fold the NCR3LG1-GPR179 pair with structural analysis to read the interface topology (extracellular versus cytoplasmic residues on each chain) and to check whether any of the 7 NCR3LG1 or 2 GPR179 glycosylation sites sit on the interface; this fold could not be run here. In particular, check whether the large interface (supplied buried surface area 4486 Å2, 1014 contacts, interface pLDDT 60.7, minimum separation 1.47 Å) involves GPR179's long, likely disordered cytoplasmic region, which would be topologically impossible for the NCR3LG1 ectodomain. 2) If the interface is ectodomain-to-ectodomain and glycosylation sites land on it, re-fold with glycans attached. 3) Confirm NCR3LG1 protein expression in retina or in ON-bipolar cell neighbours from a full expression matrix, since HPA only reports it as non-specific. 4) The supplied breadth data (1 of 6 partner receptors tested was confident; p_twoway 0.046855) suggests some specificity, but this should be confirmed with a counter-screen. 5) The other_subunits listed are documented partners of each protein from UniProt function text (NCR3 for NCR3LG1; GRM6, TRPM1 and R7 RGS-GNB5 for GPR179), not CellPhoneDB complex members (CellPhoneDB returned no complexes for either gene); they are context for a possible competition or co-complex test, not a confirmed missing subunit.

rationale: The pair is unreported (STRING not found, CellPhoneDB not found, 0 PubMed co-mentions) and both are brain-enriched plasma-membrane proteins, so an encounter is plausible. rationale: I'm withdrawing ALREADY_KNOWN. The check reports known_interaction_strength=none: STRING and CellPhoneDB have no record, and GPRC5A is missing from the CellPhoneDB table. The only support is PMID 32115889, and I read only its title. The title describes an RSK-EphA2-GPRC5A signalling switch, which could be a functional or expression axis and not a physical complex. PMID 27715394 only co-mentions EPHA2. The HPA contradiction is real. Neither protein is secreted, and they share no protein-level tissue expression in HPA, so the data give no normal-tissue route for them to meet. I don't call it IMPLAUSIBLE, because both are plasma-membrane proteins and the 2020 paper studies them together in ovarian cancer cells, which HPA's normal-tissue data would not capture. The fold status is topology_violation, so any AF3 contact is not a credible direct-binding model. EPHA2 phosphorylation by RSK, which a bare-sequence model omits, may also gate any association. The evidence supports a functional link but neither confirms nor excludes direct binding.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: EPHA2 and GPRC5A are both glycoproteins and phosphoproteins. RSK-dependent EphA2 phosphorylation may gate the association, and AF3 does not represent it. Whether any site lies on the modeled interface was not checked.
cooccurrence_evidence: 2 PubMed hits. PMID 32115889 is a dedicated paper on an RSK-EphA2-GPRC5A signalling axis in ovarian cancer chemoresistance, which is a real pair-specific hit. PMID 27715394 is a GPRC5A/integrin beta-1 adhesion paper that co-mentions EPHA2. Only titles were retrieved, so whether either reports direct binding (for example co-immunoprecipitation) was not verified here.
known_interaction_evidence: STRING and CellPhoneDB: no record (GPRC5A is not in CellPhoneDB, so that miss is uninformative). PubMed: 2 hits. PMID 32115889 is a title-level functional signalling-axis link, not confirmed physical binding. PMID 27715394 is a co-mention only. Known-interaction strength is 'none', so ALREADY_KNOWN is not supported.
follow_up: Read the abstract and results of PMID 32115889 to see whether it shows co-IP or proximity evidence for direct EphA2-GPRC5A binding. Re-fold with the correct membrane topology (EPHA2 ectodomain versus GPRC5A extracellular face) and the phosphorylated EphA2 S897 residue represented.
